findings.title: Require exact raw native event identity before ID conversion
findings.body: The native event check compares mapped IDs, although that mapping is not injective. For example, supplied event_id "a:b" accepts a native event with publicID "a b" because both become "smi:nz.org.geonet/a_b". Neither collision registry includes the supplied raw event_id, so the substituted event returns status "ok" and can establish the QML profile binding. Compare native publicID against the supplied raw identity before conversion, as required by the protocol's substituted-ID policy.

findings.title: Resolve raw arrival references before stripping candidate IDs
findings.body: Stripping the mapped arrival ID can turn a dangling raw reference into an accepted pick. Consider an arrival referencing "smi:invented/p " with no exact target, while an amplitude selects the existing pick "smi:invented/p". Selection and collision checks preserve these as distinct IDs, but this strip makes the arrival resolve to the amplitude-selected pick. analyse() then accepts it and includes it in clocks, contrary to the rule that dangling targets never establish correspondence. Require a unique exact raw pick target before using its candidate ID for acceptance.

findings.title: Calculate newly accepted NZ references against left-side NZ acceptance
findings.body: The NZ recovery counter intersects with newly_resolved, which has already removed every left-side accepted pick regardless of network. If the same left-qualified pick is accepted with network "XX" on the left and repaired to "NZ" on the right, newly accepted across networks correctly remains zero, but newly_accepted_NZ_reference_count incorrectly remains zero too. The protocol declares these as separate recovery counts. Compute the NZ gain from right-side NZ acceptance minus left-side NZ acceptance, restricted to left-qualified IDs.

overall_explanation: Native identity and reference guards can accept substituted events or dangling references, and NZ recovery accounting misses network repairs. These violate the frozen diagnostic contracts. Review used read-only source inspection; tests were not run.
